newsitem.title: FINLAND: Rauma plans to buy back one mln shares.
newsitem.headline: Rauma plans to buy back one mln shares.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Rauma Oy plans to accept the offer by Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy to redeem one million of its own shares and then cancel them, Rauma CEO Heikki Hakala said on Tuesday.
When asked at a news conference whether the company planned to exercise the opportunity to buy back one million shares, he said: "Yes, that is our intention."

UPM-Kymmene said earlier it planned to cut its stake in Rauma to around 35 percent from 60 percent by offering to domestic and foreign investors 10.5 million shares, plus a greenshoe of 1.58 million shares.
In connection with that offer, UPM said it would offer one million shares to Rauma for redemption.
With 54 million Rauma shares in issue, buying back and voiding one million shares would have a positive effect on per-share earnings of "about two percent on the yearly level," Hakala said.

Hakala spoke after Rauma reported first-quarter profits before extras and taxes down 24 percent to 158 million markka from 208 million in the year-ago period. The result was squarely in line with analysts' expectations.
Hakala said possible further share redeptions would depend entirely on earnings and cash flow, but that the company would also consider buy-backs in the future.
"If we do not find appropriate acquisitions ... then we will be willing to consider share buy-backs also in the future," Hakala said.
"If money accumulates and nothing else (to do with that money) is invented, then it is clear that this is in the interest of shareholders," he said.
"We don't know how much of of this (offering) will go to foreign investors, but I would imagine that domestic institutions and the (Finnish) public will be interested," Hakala said.

"Maybe more of this will go to domestic investors than in (Rauma's) initial public offering," he said, adding that between 30 and 40 percent of Rauma's 1995 IPO had been subscribed by Finnish investors.
In that case, the offering would be spread rather evenly among foreign and Finnish investors, Hakala said.
UPM's decision to trim its Rauma stake, which followed on the heels of a dividend payout this year to UPM shreholders partly in Rauma stock, came at a good time, Rauma executives said.
"The market situation is good. Yesterday, New York stocks reached an all-time high," said Kari Janhunen, vice president for corporate financing and investor relations.

Hakala declined to say whether Rauma's earnings this year would be better or worse than last year, only repeating an earlier forecast: "The situation is stable. We believe the full-year result will remain on a good level."
In 1996, Rauma's profit before extraordinary items, taxes and minorities rose to 679 million markka from 671 million in 1995, while earnings per share fell to 9.15 markka from 9.32 markka.
